name: a worn footpath of packed earth between shacks, lighter than the surrounding dirt, with faint wheel ruts and footprints, its edges feathering softly into the dirt with no outline, laid as a path network with crossings and dead ends
label: wasteland_ruins/track

surfaces.part: packed earth ground texture, full tile field

answer.evidence: The image is a full-bleed 256x192 terrain texture of mottled brown earth with a lighter path network, ruts and footprints. Every row has the same width of 256, so there is no silhouette, no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse and no vertical face. The column scans show only mottled noise bands of 1-25 rows with no structural step. It is flat ground seen from above, which fits the terrain kind, so no standing-object top or front face applies.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a packed-earth path with no outline, and its edges feather into the dirt as the brief asks. The measured facts show 4 visible tones per tile, against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference. Near-flat coverage is 2% and dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so there are no flat fills and no sticker outline. The soil carries speckle and clumpy dark patches, so it has grain. The weaknesses are that the path is lighter than the dirt by only about one step, so the ruts and footprints barely read, and that the soil's dark swirl pattern repeats tile to tile. The result is about 4 tones, roughly 4 shading steps against the references' 5-6, with only 6 distinct colours in total. A careful artist would find it somewhat thinner than the Beodeul references, with fewer tones and less per-clump shading. It is close but not clearly at the reference level, so I fail it on the when-in-doubt rule.
